memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'On the eighth day he must take two doves or two young pigeons and come before the LORD to the entrance to the tent of meeting and give them to the priest. The priest is to sacrifice them, the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering. In this way he will make atonement before the LORD for the man because of his discharge.'" - Lev 15:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two birds, and atonement made. Note the offering: two doves or pigeons — the offering of the poor. God set the requirement low, because this could happen to anyone.

But again the question arises: why a sin offering for an illness? He had done nothing wrong.

The answer is not that his sickness was sin. It is that no one, in any condition, approaches a holy God without atonement. This chapter keeps teaching the same lesson from different angles: the gap between God and us is not something we cross by being well, or by being good, or by waiting long enough.

That is humbling, and it is also freeing. It means the healthy person had no advantage over the sick one. Everyone came to the same altar. Everyone needed the same blood.

For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and all are justified freely by his grace through the redemption that came by Christ Jesus (Rom 3:23-24). The same "all" in both halves of the sentence.

You do not approach God today because your circumstances have improved. You approach through the blood of Jesus — which is why you can approach at all, on your best day and your worst.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you feel more acceptable to God when life is going well?
2. What does it mean that everyone comes to the same altar?
3. How does resting in Christ's atonement steady you today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that my access to You rests on Christ's blood and not on my circumstances. Let me come to You freely today, whatever state I am in. Amen.
